pm.metric.Q_PORTAO.title: Current phase gate
pm.metric.Q_PORTAO.advice: Close the exit criteria before requesting the gate review: each phase ends at a gate, and governance decides.
pm.metric.Q_EAP_100.title: WBS 100% rule
pm.metric.Q_EAP_100.detail: {n} issue(s): children do not add up to the parent or an activity is outside a work package.
pm.metric.Q_EAP_100.advice: Link each activity to a work package (leaf) and make children add up to the parent: nothing more, nothing less.
pm.metric.Q_EAP_SUBSTANTIVOS.title: WBS decomposes deliverables
pm.metric.Q_EAP_SUBSTANTIVOS.advice: The WBS decomposes deliverables (nouns), not activities (verbs): "Test integration" becomes "Integration test report".
pm.metric.Q_RACI.title: RACI matrix
pm.metric.Q_RACI.detail: {n} of {total} activities without exactly one A or without an R.
pm.metric.Q_RACI.advice: There can be only one A per activity: if two people are accountable, nobody is. R can be shared.
pm.metric.Q_RASTREABILIDADE.title: Requirements traceability
pm.metric.Q_RASTREABILIDADE.advice: Link each requirement to its origin, deliverable and test: it is the antidote to scope creep.
pm.metric.Q_GOLD_PLATING.title: Gold plating
pm.metric.Q_GOLD_PLATING.detail: {n} deliverable(s) with no requirement behind them.
pm.metric.Q_GOLD_PLATING.advice: A deliverable no requirement asks for is work beyond what was agreed: link it to a requirement or drop it.
pm.metric.Q_CRONOGRAMA.title: Critical path
pm.metric.Q_CRONOGRAMA.detail: {finish} days · {critical} of {total} activities on the critical path ({share}%).
pm.metric.Q_CRONOGRAMA.advice: With almost everything critical there is no float: consider fast tracking or crashing.
pm.metric.Q_PERT.title: Probability of meeting the deadline (PERT)
pm.metric.Q_PERT.detail: {probability}% chance of finishing in {target} days; P80 = {p80} days.
pm.metric.Q_PERT.advice: With low probability, renegotiate the deadline against the baseline or reduce uncertainty on critical activities (high σ).
pm.metric.Q_IDC.title: Cost performance (CPI)
pm.metric.Q_IDC.advice: CPI < 1 means each unit spent earned less than one unit of work: review spending before the EAC overruns.
pm.metric.Q_IDP.title: Schedule performance (SPI)
pm.metric.Q_IDP.advice: SPI < 1 is behind the baseline: tackle late critical activities first.
pm.metric.Q_RESERVA.title: Reserve × risks (EMV)
pm.metric.Q_RESERVA.advice: The contingency reserve (known risks) should cover the net EMV; the management reserve stays outside the baseline.
pm.metric.Q_RISCOS_RESPOSTA.title: Risk responses
pm.metric.Q_RISCOS_RESPOSTA.detail: {n} open risk(s) without a planned response.
pm.metric.Q_RISCOS_RESPOSTA.advice: Every threat needs a response: avoid, transfer, mitigate or accept (with reserve).
pm.metric.Q_SCOPE_CREEP.title: Scope creep
pm.metric.Q_SCOPE_CREEP.detail: {n} activity(ies) created after the baseline without an approved change: {codes}.
pm.metric.Q_SCOPE_CREEP.advice: Record it as a change request, analyse impact on the six constraints and take it to the board; only then update the baseline.
pm.metric.Q_MUDANCAS_ANALISE.title: Change analysis
pm.metric.Q_MUDANCAS_ANALISE.detail: {n} of {open} open change(s) missing the 7 Rs or an impact estimate.
pm.metric.Q_MUDANCAS_ANALISE.advice: Before the board: raised by, reason, return, risks, resources, responsible and relationship to other changes.
pm.metric.Q_LICOES.title: Lessons learned throughout
pm.metric.Q_LICOES.detail: Recorded in {phases} of {elapsed} phases ({total} in total).
pm.metric.Q_LICOES.advice: Record lessons in every phase, not only at the end: by closing the memory is gone.
pm.metric.G_ALINHAMENTO.title: Goals cascade
pm.metric.G_ALINHAMENTO.detail: {aligned} of {total} objective(s) linked to the strategic plan.
pm.metric.G_ALINHAMENTO.advice: No IT goal stands alone: link each project objective to a strategic objective (top-down).
pm.metric.G_SMART.title: SMART objectives
pm.metric.G_SMART.detail: {smart} of {total} objective(s) specific, measurable and time-bound.
pm.metric.G_SMART.advice: An objective says where; a target says how much and by when. Rewrite with a number and a date.
pm.metric.G_TAP_PATROCINADOR.title: Charter approved by the sponsor
pm.metric.G_TAP_PATROCINADOR.detail: The charter is approved by the sponsor, not by the project manager.
pm.metric.G_TAP_PATROCINADOR.advice: Ask the sponsor for formal approval: without a charter the project does not officially exist.
pm.metric.G_GUT.title: Demand priority (GUT)
pm.metric.G_GUT.advice: Rate gravity, urgency and trend from 1 to 5; priority is the product, not the sum.
pm.metric.G_DECISOES_PORTAO.title: Gates decided in DECIA
pm.metric.G_DECISOES_PORTAO.detail: {inDecia} of {total} gate(s) decided with a DECIA record.
pm.metric.G_DECISOES_PORTAO.advice: Governance decides and holds to account; management plans and does. Take each gate to DECIA to keep the why and the snapshot.
pm.metric.G_DECISOES_MUDANCA.title: Changes decided by the board
pm.metric.G_DECISOES_MUDANCA.detail: {inDecia} of {total} normal change(s) decided in DECIA.
pm.metric.G_DECISOES_MUDANCA.advice: A normal change goes through the board (CCB/CAB); record the decision in DECIA.
pm.metric.G_ISO38500.title: ISO/IEC 38500 principles
pm.metric.G_ISO38500.advice: Responsibility, strategy, acquisition, performance, conformance and human behaviour — the last is the most forgotten.
pm.metric.G_RUN_GROW_TRANSFORM.title: Run · Grow · Transform
pm.metric.G_RUN_GROW_TRANSFORM.advice: The larger the Run share, the less room to support strategy; use it as the executive reading of the budget.
pm.metric.G_ACORDOS_SERVICO.title: SLA × OLA × underpinning contract
pm.metric.G_ACORDOS_SERVICO.detail: SLA {sla} h · OLA {ola} h · contract {uc} h.
pm.metric.G_ACORDOS_SERVICO.advice: OLAs and supplier contracts must be stricter than the SLA they support.
pm.metric.G_AUTORIDADE_GP.title: Project manager authority
pm.metric.G_AUTORIDADE_GP.advice: In functional or weak matrix structures the PM coordinates without formal authority: agree with the functional manager who releases resources.
pm.metric.W_CARGA.title: Workload distribution
pm.metric.W_CARGA.detail: {share}% of work-days on a single person ({people} of {team} with activities).
pm.metric.W_CARGA.advice: Redistribute activities: high concentration delays the group and hides what only one person knows.
pm.metric.W_CRITICO_CONCENTRADO.title: Critical path on a single person
pm.metric.W_CRITICO_CONCENTRADO.detail: {share}% of the {critical} critical activities with the same person.
pm.metric.W_CRITICO_CONCENTRADO.advice: If that person is absent, the whole project slips: split or support the critical activities.
pm.metric.W_QUATRO_OLHOS.title: Review by someone else
pm.metric.W_QUATRO_OLHOS.detail: {reviewed} of {done} completed deliverables reviewed by someone other than the owner.
pm.metric.W_QUATRO_OLHOS.advice: Ask someone else to review before completing: quality is controlled with four eyes.
pm.metric.W_SEM_RESPONSAVEL.title: Activities without an owner
pm.metric.W_SEM_RESPONSAVEL.advice: Ownerless work does not move: assign a responsible (R) and an accountable (A).
pm.metric.W_PARTICIPACAO_EDICOES.title: Who builds the plan
pm.metric.W_PARTICIPACAO_EDICOES.detail: {authors} of {team} team members made changes to the project.
pm.metric.W_PARTICIPACAO_EDICOES.advice: A plan made by one person is that person's plan: bring the team into the canvas and the board.
pm.metric.W_PARTICIPACAO_DECISOES.title: Participation in decisions

pm.metric.W_PARTICIPACAO_DECISOES.advice: Ask each participant for an independent assessment before deciding: it avoids herding.

pm.board.modelHint.INSTITUCIONAL: Seven institutional life-cycle phases (demand → closing), each ending at a gate.
pm.board.modelHint.PMBOK: Four classic phases: initiating, planning, executing and closing; planning groups elaboration, analysis and approval.
pm.board.modelHint.SCRUM: Sprint flow (product backlog → done); in hybrid projects, sprints run inside execution.
pm.board.theory1: Columns are life-cycle PHASES, not process groups: the five groups (initiating, planning, executing, monitoring and controlling, closing) recur in every phase — each column shows the dominant one.
pm.board.theory2: Monitoring and controlling cuts across everything: it is not a column but the band below the board, tracking earned value, changes, risks and lessons in every phase.
pm.board.theory3: Each phase ends at a gate with verifiable exit criteria. Governance decides whether to pass (EDM; ISO 38500: evaluate, direct, monitor), in DECIA; the work inside the phase is management (APO, BAI, DSS, MEA).
pm.board.gateHint: The system checks the criteria; the decision to pass belongs to governance and is recorded in DECIA.
pm.board.decidedOutside: Decided outside DECIA: there is no record of who decided, on which criteria and why.

pm.task.pert.problem.PESSIMISTA_MENOR_QU: Pessimistic cannot be lower than optimistic.

pm.tl.rebaselineHint: The baseline only changes through an approved change (integrated change control); re-baselining without one hides variances.
pm.tl.cycleTitle: The schedule network has a cycle
pm.tl.cycle: Cycle: {codes}. CPM needs an acyclic network — remove one of the links in the canvas or in the dependencies.
pm.tl.pert.title: PERT — how likely are we to meet the deadline?
pm.tl.pert.noVariance: No three-point estimates on the critical path: the deadline is deterministic. Enter O, M and P on critical activities to measure schedule risk.
pm.tl.pert.theory: TE = (O + 4M + P) / 6 and σ = (P − O) / 6 per activity; along the critical path TEs and variances (σ²) add up. Z = (deadline − TE) / σ gives the probability from the normal distribution.
pm.tl.curve.title: S-curve and earned value
pm.tl.curve.desc: At the status date: PV {pv}, EV {ev}, AC {ac}; BAC {bac}.
pm.tl.curve.theory: The S-curve accumulates planned value (PV). At the status date, EV below PV means delay (SPI = EV/PV < 1) and AC above EV means cost overrun (CPI = EV/AC < 1).
pm.tl.net.title: Network diagram (activity on node)
pm.tl.net.key: In each node: top ES · duration · EF; bottom LS · total float · LF. Red border = critical path (zero float).
pm.tl.net.theory: Forward pass: ES = largest EF of the predecessors; backward pass: LF = smallest LS of the successors. Total float = LS − ES; critical path = the zero-float chain.

pm.tl.deps.title: Network dependencies
pm.tl.deps.theory: Finish → start is the most common; start → start, finish → finish and start → finish also exist. A positive lag waits; a negative one is a lead.

pm.ctl.evm.read.noAc: No actual cost recorded: CPI and EAC do not exist yet.
pm.ctl.evm.read.noPv: PV is zero at the status date: SPI does not exist yet.
pm.ctl.evm.rule: Reading rule: for variances (CV, SV), positive is good; for indices (CPI, SPI), above 1 is good.
pm.ctl.evm.theory: Earned value combines scope, schedule and cost in a single picture: it compares the work done (EV) with the work planned (PV) and with what was spent (AC). Which EAC? Typical, when current cost performance will continue; atypical, when the variance was a one-off and the rest follows the budget; composite, when cost and schedule weigh together.
pm.ctl.base.title: Baseline
pm.ctl.base.set: Approved on {date} · finish in {finish} days · BAC {bac}
pm.ctl.base.none: No baseline: PV uses the current schedule, which changes with every edit — deviations become invisible.
pm.ctl.base.what: The baseline freezes the approved schedule (start, finish and duration of each activity) and budget: PV, BAC and the S-curve come from it. It only changes through an approved change — “Implement” on a change already updates it. If it moved with every delay, the variance would vanish and control would lose its reference.
pm.ctl.base.dialogBody: The current plan becomes the earned value reference: {n} activities, finish in {finish} days, BAC {bac}.
pm.ctl.base.why: Re-planning is a formal decision: outside the change flow, only with the sponsor's or the committee's approval.
pm.ctl.base.creepWarning: Warning: {codes} would enter the baseline without an approved change — that legalises scope creep. Regularise it first through change control.
pm.ctl.progress.title: Progress update
pm.ctl.progress.hint: Enter each activity's % complete and actual cost: the earned value above is recalculated immediately.
pm.ctl.progress.caption: Activity progress: status, % complete, budget, actual cost and earned value
pm.ctl.chg.title: Integrated change control
pm.ctl.chg.theory: No change slips in “by surprise”: every change to scope, schedule or cost becomes a formal request, has its impact analysed and is approved or rejected; only then does the baseline change and stakeholders are informed. Accepting without analysis is scope creep.
pm.ctl.chg.types: Types (ITIL): standard is pre-approved, low-risk and follows a known procedure — it skips the CAB; normal is assessed by the committee (CCB/CAB); emergency is assessed urgently by the ECAB. Before the committee, the 7 Rs: who raised it, reason, return, risks, resources, responsible and relationship with other changes.
pm.ctl.chg.impactHint: Scope, quality, resources and risks from 0 (none) to 5 (very high); schedule in days and cost in reais (negative = reduction).
pm.ctl.chg.incomplete: Incomplete analysis: {n} of the 7 Rs missing.
pm.ctl.chg.noImpact: Impact not estimated yet: the committee does not decide in the dark.
pm.ctl.chg.normalHint: A normal change is the committee's decision: take it to DECIA to record the why and the snapshot. Deciding here counts as an unrecorded decision.
pm.ctl.chg.toCommittee: Take to the committee (CCB/CAB) in DECIA
pm.ctl.chg.noDecision: Decided without a record in DECIA: the reason for the decision is not traceable.
pm.ctl.chg.implementHint: Creates the activity linked to the change in the current phase ({phase}) and updates the baseline; then fit it into the schedule and the budget.
pm.ctl.chg.implementRegularizeHint: The work already exists: implementing updates the baseline to include it, and the scope creep alert is closed.
pm.ctl.chg.final: Final state: nothing else to do on this request.
pm.ctl.creep.title: Scope creep
pm.ctl.creep.noBaseline: Without a baseline there is no way to measure scope creep: approve the baseline first.
pm.ctl.creep.none: No activity outside the baseline without an approved change.
pm.ctl.creep.detail: Created after the baseline without an approved change · {phase} · {status} · AC {ac}
pm.ctl.creep.relationship: Regularises activity {code}, created after the baseline without an approved change.
pm.ctl.creep.regularized: Regularised by {code}: it enters the next approved baseline.
pm.ctl.creep.rejected: Change {code} was rejected: undo the out-of-scope work or open a new request.
pm.ctl.creep.vsGold: Scope creep × gold plating: scope creep is accepting informal requests (usually from the client) without going through change control; gold plating is the team itself delivering more than was asked. Both escape the approved scope — requirements traceability and integrated change control are the antidote.
pm.ctl.lessons.title: Lessons learned throughout the project
pm.ctl.lessons.coverage: Lessons in {phases} of {elapsed} phases so far
pm.ctl.lessons.missing: Phases so far without a lesson: {phases}.
pm.ctl.lessons.placeholder: What worked or not, and what to do next time
pm.ctl.lessons.theory: Classic mistake: collecting lessons only at the end. Record them in every phase (and every sprint): by closing time the memory is gone. Lessons become organisational process assets for future projects.
pm.ctl.history.title: Version history
pm.ctl.history.hint: {n} versions: every structural change creates one, with author and date (RF22.CA02).
pm.close.title: Closing
pm.close.intro: Closing means formalising, not just finishing the work — it also applies to cancelled projects. Then the product becomes a service and moves into operations.
pm.close.formal.title: Formal closure
pm.close.formal.acceptanceHint: The client or sponsor states in writing that they received what was agreed. Without acceptance, the project does not close.
pm.close.formal.contractsClosedHint: Procurements and supplier contracts formally closed.
pm.close.formal.resourcesReleasedHint: Team and physical resources returned or reassigned.
pm.close.formal.finalReportHint: The final documentation is stored: it is the project's memory for audits and for future projects.
pm.close.formal.theory: Closure is not a synonym for success, it is formalisation. A cancelled project also goes through formal closure: you record why it was stopped and which lessons remain.
pm.close.cancel.label: Cancellation reason
pm.close.cancel.hint: Fill in only if the project was cancelled or stopped: it is also closed formally, with the reason and the lessons.
pm.close.archive.title: Archiving
pm.close.archive.archived: Project archived: read-only (RF22.CA06). No structural change is accepted until it is reopened.
pm.close.archive.active: Active project: archive it after acceptance and the final report.
pm.close.archive.dialogBody: The project becomes read-only (RF22.CA06): no structural change is accepted until someone reopens it.
pm.close.archive.ready: All Closing gate criteria are met.
pm.close.archive.reopenHint: Reopening is allowed even when the project is archived and is recorded in the version history.
pm.close.gate.title: Closing gate
pm.close.gate.notYet: The final review in DECIA becomes available when the project reaches the Closing phase (current phase: {phase}).
pm.close.gate.theory: Each phase ends at a gate with verifiable exit criteria. The decision to close belongs to governance (evaluate, direct, monitor) and is recorded in DECIA, with the reason.
pm.close.service.title: Transition to operations (ITIL)
pm.close.service.intro: A project is temporary, operations are ongoing: before closing, the service enters the catalogue, the service desk receives the knowledge and the CMDB records the configuration items.
pm.close.service.cancelled: Cancelled project: the transition to operations is no longer a gate criterion, but record whatever is already in production.
pm.close.service.slaHint: Agreement between the IT provider and the client or business: promised restoration time, in hours.
pm.close.service.olaHint: Internal agreement with another team that supports the SLA, in hours.
pm.close.service.ucHint: Underpinning contract with an external supplier, legally binding, in hours.
pm.close.service.compareTitle: Restoration time promised in each agreement
pm.close.service.problem.OLA_MENOS_RIGID: An OLA of {ola} h is not stricter than the {sla} h SLA: the internal team must restore before the deadline promised to the client.
pm.close.service.problem.UC_MENOS_RIGIDO: An underpinning contract (UC) of {uc} h is not stricter than the {sla} h SLA: the supplier must respond before the deadline promised to the client.
pm.close.service.ok: OLA and UC stricter than the SLA: the agreements hold up.
pm.close.service.noSla: Set the SLA to validate the OLA and the underpinning contract.
pm.close.service.catalogEntryHint: The service is shown to users with what it offers and its service level (service design).
pm.close.service.knowledgeBaseHint: The service desk receives procedures, known errors and workarounds (knowledge management).
pm.close.service.cmdbUpdatedHint: Configuration items and their relationships recorded: this is what allows the impact of future changes to be analysed.
pm.close.service.theory: SLA (client) × OLA (internal team) × UC (supplier): the OLA and the UC must be stricter than the SLA they support. If you promise the client a 4 h restoration, the supplier contract cannot allow 6 h.
pm.close.service.transitionTheory: Service transition (ITIL): going live without breaking anything — change management, configuration (CMDB), release and knowledge management. Building the platform is a project; sustaining it afterwards is operations.
pm.close.lessons.title: Lessons learned
pm.close.lessons.intro: {n} lesson(s), by phase and type: they become organisational process assets for future projects.
pm.close.lessons.theory: Lessons are collected throughout the project, not only at the end: closing consolidates what was already recorded in each phase.
pm.close.report.title: Final report
pm.close.report.intro: Assembled by the system from the model — review it and copy it into the final document.
pm.close.report.copyFailed: Could not copy: select the report text and copy it manually.
pm.close.report.heading: Final report — {title}
pm.close.report.scheduleLine: Calculated finish: {finish} days ({date}) · baseline: {baseline} days ({baselineDate}) · variance: {delta} day(s)
pm.close.report.scheduleNoBaseline: Calculated finish: {finish} days ({date}) · no baseline to compare
pm.close.report.scheduleCycle: Schedule with a cycle: finish undefined.
pm.close.report.requirements: Complete requirements (origin, deliverable and test): {complete} of {total}
pm.close.report.changes: Changes: {approved} approved awaiting implementation · {implemented} implemented · {rejected} rejected · {open} open
pm.close.report.lessonsLine: {total} lesson(s): {positive} that worked and {negative} that did not, in {phases} phase(s)
pm.close.report.closureLine: Formal acceptance: {acceptance} · contracts closed: {contracts} · resources released: {resources} · final report: {report}
pm.close.report.serviceLine: SLA {sla} h · OLA {ola} h · UC {uc} h · catalogue: {catalog} · knowledge base: {knowledge} · CMDB: {cmdb}
pm.tl.mc.title: Monte Carlo schedule simulation
pm.tl.mc.stale: Result from version {n}: the project changed, simulate again.
pm.tl.mc.none: No uncertainty to simulate: enter optimistic, most likely and pessimistic (O, M, P) on the activities.
pm.tl.mc.vsPert: Analytic PERT (critical path only): TE {te} d, {p}
pm.tl.mc.theory: Each scenario draws durations from the Beta-PERT (mean = TE) and recomputes the network. Analytic PERT looks only at the critical path and ignores merge bias: near-critical paths that, once drawn, become critical — which is why simulation usually yields a later finish. The criticality index shows in how many scenarios each activity was on the critical path.

pm.scope.gate.title: Gates tied to scope
pm.scope.gate.hint: Exit criteria checked by the system: the WBS counts at the Planning gate; traceability and gold plating at the Elaboration gate.
pm.scope.issue.PARECE_ATIVIDADE: Looks like an activity (verb), not a deliverable
pm.scope.issue.PARECE_ATIVIDADE.fix: The WBS breaks down deliverables (nouns): rename it after the product — "Test integration" becomes "Integration test report".
pm.scope.issue.PACOTE_SEM_ATIVIDADE.fix: Nobody will produce this deliverable: link an activity to it (alongside) or create the activity on the board.
pm.scope.issue.ATIVIDADE_FORA_DO_PACOTE: linked to {node}, which is not a work package (leaf)
{code} is linked here, but activities belong to a work package (leaf)
pm.scope.wbs.title: WBS — work breakdown structure
pm.scope.wbs.lead: Hierarchical breakdown of deliverables down to the work package (leaf). The rollup climbs from the leaves: the budget declared on the package or, without it, the sum of the linked activities.
pm.scope.wbs.removeCascade: Remove {item} and {n} sub-deliverable(s)? {tasks} activity(ies) lose their package and requirements lose the link.
pm.scope.wbs.acceptancePlaceholder: How the client checks the deliverable is done
pm.scope.wbs.clearDeclared: Clear the declared budget (use the activities')
pm.scope.wbs.theory100: 100% rule: the children add up to 100% of the parent's work — no more (extra work), no less. The lowest level is the work package, described in the WBS dictionary (acceptance criterion, owner). The WBS is neither a schedule nor an org chart: it shows no sequence or dates.
pm.scope.wbs.theoryNouns: The WBS breaks down deliverables (nouns), not activities (verbs). Activities come later, in the schedule, and each one stems from a work package.
pm.scope.orphans.title: Activities outside the WBS
pm.scope.orphans.lead: Every activity produces a work package. Link each one to the package (leaf) it delivers.
pm.scope.orphans.none: All activities are in work packages.
pm.scope.orphans.creep: after the baseline with no approved change
pm.scope.orphans.creepHint: Linking {code} to a package does not authorize the work: it is scope creep until it becomes an approved change request.
pm.scope.req.title: Requirements
pm.scope.req.lead: Each requirement needs an origin (why it exists), a deliverable (where it is met) and a test (how it is verified). The boxes link the requirement to the WBS work packages.
pm.scope.req.testPlaceholder: Test case or criterion, e.g. CT-01
pm.scope.req.noLeaves: Create work packages in the WBS to link the requirement.
pm.scope.trace.title: Traceability matrix
pm.scope.trace.lead: Projection of the requirements above: where each came from, where it is delivered and how it is verified. A requirement without a deliverable or a test risks not being met; a deliverable without a requirement is extra work.
pm.scope.trace.caption: Traceability matrix: requirement, origin, WBS deliverables, test and status
pm.scope.trace.untracedHint: On the requirement card, tick the work package that meets it.
pm.scope.trace.untestedHint: Without a test there is no way to prove acceptance: record the test case or criterion.
pm.scope.trace.goldPlating: Possible gold plating (deliverable without a requirement)
pm.scope.trace.goldHint: Link it to a requirement that justifies it or take it out of scope.
pm.scope.trace.theory: The traceability matrix links each requirement to its origin (client need, business objective) and to its destination (WBS deliverable and test case). It ensures every requirement is met and that nothing out of scope gets in.
pm.scope.trace.theoryGold: Gold plating: the team itself delivers more than was asked, on its own initiative (a deliverable with no requirement). Scope creep: scope swells with requests accepted outside integrated change control. Either way the work was never approved — and the traceability matrix exposes both.
pm.scope.moscow.title: MoSCoW prioritization of activities
pm.scope.moscow.lead: Classify each activity; each group's planned days show how much of the time is already committed to the essentials.
pm.scope.moscow.hint.MUST: without it the delivery has no value
pm.scope.moscow.hint.SHOULD: important, but there is a workaround
pm.scope.moscow.hint.COULD: nice to have: in if time allows
pm.scope.moscow.hint.WONT: agreed to stay out this time
pm.scope.moscow.label: MoSCoW priority of {code}
pm.scope.moscow.theory: MoSCoW: Must (mandatory), Should (important), Could (desirable), Won't (out this time). In a timebox — the Scrum sprint — the deadline is fixed and scope is what flexes: cut from the bottom up (Won't, Could, Should), never the Must. The Product Owner prioritizes the backlog. DSDM recommends keeping Must under about 60% of the effort, to leave room to negotiate.
pm.rt.risk.title: Risk register
pm.rt.risk.lead: Identify, analyze and plan the response: the P × I matrix prioritizes (qualitative analysis) and the EMV puts the risk in money (quantitative). Threats and opportunities have different responses.
pm.rt.risk.caption: Risk register sorted by severity (P × I) and EMV
pm.rt.risk.col.title: Risk
pm.rt.risk.levelHint: In the matrix: level {n} of 5 (up to 10%, 30%, 50%, 70% and above).
pm.rt.risk.filtered: Filtered by cell P {p} × I {i}: {n} risk(s).
pm.rt.risk.emvLegend: EMV = probability × financial impact · P × I = probability level × impact level (1 to 25)
pm.rt.risk.field.title: Risk
pm.rt.risk.responses.AMEACA: Threat: avoid, transfer, mitigate or accept.
pm.rt.risk.responses.OPORTUNIDADE: Opportunity: exploit, share, enhance or accept.
pm.rt.risk.theoryResponses: Threat: avoid (remove the cause), transfer (insurance, contract), mitigate (reduce P or I) or accept (with a reserve). Opportunity: exploit (make sure it happens), share (with whoever can best seize it), enhance (raise P or I) or accept.
pm.rt.matrix.title: Probability × impact matrix
pm.rt.matrix.hint: Number of risks per cell; click a cell to filter the register.
pm.rt.matrix.caption: 5 × 5 matrix: risks by probability level (rows) and impact level (columns), with each cell's severity band
pm.rt.matrix.axes: Rows: probability (5 = most likely). Columns: impact (5 = most severe).
pm.rt.matrix.theory: Qualitative analysis: prioritizes risks by probability × impact, on 1-to-5 levels — the risk matrix. Quantitative analysis puts numbers on it: EMV = probability × financial impact (e.g. 30% × R$ 50,000 = R$ 15,000). Plan the responses for the high and critical bands first.
pm.rt.reserve.title: Exposure × reserve
pm.rt.reserve.lead: Net exposure (EMV of threats − EMV of opportunities, open risks only) sizes the contingency reserve.
pm.rt.reserve.contingencyHint: Known risks · inside the cost baseline · managed by the PM
pm.rt.reserve.managementHint: Unknown risks · outside the baseline · released by management or the sponsor
pm.rt.reserve.question: Does the contingency reserve cover the EMV?
pm.rt.reserve.noExposure: No net exposure to cover: opportunities offset the open threats.
pm.rt.reserve.composition: Cost baseline = activities {work} + contingency {contingency} = {baseline} · total budget = baseline + management {management} = {total}
pm.rt.reserve.theory: Budget: estimate each package's cost (bottom-up), aggregate it and add the contingency reserve — for the known risks — to form the cost baseline. The management reserve covers the unknowns: it stays outside the baseline and only enters the total budget; using it requires management approval.
pm.rt.stk.title: Stakeholders
pm.rt.stk.lead: Register with power (influence) and interest from 1 to 5; the Mendelow grid gives each one's engagement strategy.
pm.rt.stk.caption: Stakeholder register: name, role, power, interest and strategy
pm.rt.stk.col.name: Name
pm.rt.stk.gridCaption: Power × interest grid: stakeholders by quadrant and engagement strategy
pm.rt.stk.theory: High power and high interest: manage closely. High power, low interest: keep satisfied. Low power, high interest: keep informed. Both low: monitor. The document that details stakeholders is the stakeholder register — not the project charter.
pm.rt.team.title: Project team
pm.rt.raci.title: Team and RACI matrix
pm.rt.raci.lead: One row per activity, one column per person. Rule: exactly one A per row and at least one R; R and A may be the same person.
pm.rt.raci.summary: {n} of {total} activity(ies) with a RACI problem
pm.rt.raci.caption: Editable RACI matrix: activities in rows, people in columns and each row's diagnosis
pm.rt.raci.RA: R + A · does it and answers for it
pm.rt.raci.ok: one A, at least one R
pm.rt.raci.theory: R (responsible) does the work — there may be more than one. A (accountable) answers for the result and approves — always exactly one: if two people answer, nobody does. C is consulted before (two-way); I is informed after (one-way).
pm.rt.assign.title: Owner, reviewer and workload
pm.rt.assign.lead: Who carries out each activity and who reviews the deliverable before it is closed; alongside, each person's days of work.
pm.rt.assign.caption: Owner and reviewer per activity, with the four-eyes check
pm.rt.assign.theory: Whoever did it does not review it: review by someone else (four eyes) is quality control and segregation of duties — no code of ethics replaces that control.
pm.rt.load.title: Workload per person
pm.rt.load.hint: Assigned days of work: the sum of the durations of the activities the person owns (milestones don't count). The bar shows each one's share of the assigned total.
pm.rt.load.theory: Workload concentrated on one person delays the group and hides what only they know: redistribute activities and, on the critical path, back up whoever holds the zero float.
pm.rt.gates.title: Gates tied to risks and team
pm.rt.gates.hint: Planning weighs the RACI, the risk analysis and a reserve that covers the EMV; Analysis weighs the response to high and critical risks.

pm.ini.subtitle: Initiating process group: this is where the project is formally born — approach, project charter, objectives, business case and the Demand gate.
pm.ini.metricsHint: The same numbers as the AI feedback, computed from the project.
pm.ini.approach.title: Life cycle approach
pm.ini.approach.label: Project approach
pm.ini.approach.when.PREDITIVO: When to use: stable, well-known requirements; scope, schedule and cost defined up front, with a single delivery at the end.
pm.ini.approach.when.ITERATIVO: When to use: partially clear requirements; the product is refined or delivered in successive parts.
pm.ini.approach.when.AGIL: When to use: volatile requirements and the need to deliver value early; short iterations, frequent deliveries and flexible scope (Scrum).
pm.ini.approach.when.HIBRIDO: When to use: stable components alongside uncertain ones; combines predictive and agile parts.
pm.ini.approach.effect.PREDITIVO: In the workspace: phase board (institutional or PMBOK); scope stays in the baseline and only changes through the committee.
pm.ini.approach.effect.ITERATIVO: In the workspace: the Scrum board covers every activity, organized in sprints.
pm.ini.approach.effect.AGIL: In the workspace: the Scrum board covers every activity — product backlog, current sprint and done.
pm.ini.approach.effect.HIBRIDO: In the workspace: predictive phases up to approval; in Execution, the Scrum board organizes activities in sprints.
pm.ini.approach.mismatchAgile: {approach} approach with the board set to “{board}”: the Scrum flow shows the product backlog and the current sprint.
pm.ini.approach.mismatchPredictive: Predictive approach with the board in Scrum flow: that flow only shows Execution activities.
pm.ini.approach.theory: Predictive × agile is the axis the exam always tests: in predictive, scope is fixed up front and change is costly; in agile, scope evolves each iteration and change is expected. Hybrid combines both in the same project.
pm.ini.tap.title: Project charter
pm.ini.tap.subtitle: Formally authorizes the project and names the project manager, with authority to use organizational resources. It is high level.
pm.ini.tap.productHint: The unique product, service or result the project delivers.
pm.ini.tap.notApproved: No formal sponsor approval yet: without an approved charter the project does not officially exist.
pm.ini.tap.approveBlockedNoSponsor: Set the sponsor to record the approval.
pm.ini.tap.approveBlockedSame: The sponsor cannot be the project manager: choose who sponsors the project.
pm.ini.tap.summaryBudgetHint: High-level overall amount; the line-item budget belongs to planning.
pm.ini.tap.linesTotal: Charter: {tap} · sum of the budget lines (Governance tab): {lines}.
pm.ini.tap.hint.justification: Why the project exists: the problem or the opportunity.
pm.ini.tap.hint.highLevelRequirements: High level; detail and traceability come in planning.
pm.ini.tap.hint.premises: What is assumed true without proof (e.g. a dedicated team).
pm.ini.tap.hint.constraints: Limits imposed on the project: maximum budget, legal deadline, regulation.
pm.ini.tap.hint.highLevelRisks: Initial risks; the detailed analysis goes in the risk register.
pm.ini.tap.hint.teamRoles: Roles needed (Team block of the Project Model Canvas).
pm.ini.tap.hint.milestones: High-level schedule milestones; the detailed schedule belongs to planning.
pm.ini.tap.theorySponsor: The charter formally authorizes the project and names the project manager; without it the project does not officially exist. It is signed by the sponsor (or initiator) — not the PM.
pm.ini.tap.theoryPlan: Charter × project management plan: the charter authorizes and sets the overall direction; the plan details how to execute. WBS, full schedule and line-item budget do not go in the charter — they are planning.
pm.ini.diag.title: Charter diagnosis
pm.ini.diag.sameSponsor: Sponsor and project manager are the same person ({name}). The charter is approved by the sponsor, not the PM — a common mistake.
pm.ini.diag.noSponsor: No sponsor set: nobody can approve the charter.
pm.ini.diag.noManager: No project manager assigned: the charter names the PM and sets their authority.
pm.ini.diag.approvedInvalid: The recorded approval is not valid: it must come from a sponsor who is not the project manager.
pm.ini.diag.notApproved: Charter not yet approved by the sponsor.
pm.ini.diag.noObjectives: The charter has no objectives: write measurable objectives.
pm.ini.diag.notSmart: {n} objective(s) without the SMART criteria: {list}. Rewrite with a number and a deadline.
pm.ini.diag.noGoal: {n} objective(s) with no strategic goal: {list}. Link them in the goals cascade.
pm.ini.diag.allGood: Consistent charter: sponsor other than the PM, approval recorded and SMART objectives aligned with the strategy.
pm.ini.content.title: What goes in the charter
pm.ini.obj.title: SMART objectives
pm.ini.obj.subtitle: An objective says where to; a target says how much and by when. Mark SMART only when the text has a number and a deadline, and link each objective to a strategic goal.
pm.ini.obj.noGoalsYet: No strategic goals yet: bring in the strategic plan in Governance.
pm.ini.obj.theory: An objective says where to; a (SMART) target says how much and by when; an indicator says how to know; an action says what to do. E.g. “Reach 99.5% availability by Dec/2027”.
pm.ini.smart.title: The five SMART criteria
pm.ini.smart.M: Measurable: has a number or an indicator.
pm.ini.smart.A: Achievable: feasible with the project's resources.
pm.ini.bc.title: Business case
pm.ini.bc.subtitle: Economic justification: why is the investment worth it? It comes before the charter and grounds it.
pm.ini.bc.rate: Discount rate (minimum attractive rate of return)
pm.ini.bc.rateHint: In % per year; discounts future cash flows in the NPV.
pm.ini.bc.caption: Cash flows per year, cumulative, present value and discounted cumulative
pm.ini.bc.year0Positive: Year 0 is usually the investment (a negative value): check the sign.
pm.ini.bc.needTwo: Enter the investment (year 0) and at least one year of return to assess viability.
pm.ini.bc.noPayback: does not pay back within the horizon
pm.ini.bc.formula.irr: IRR = the rate i that makes NPV = 0
pm.ini.bc.formula.payback: time until the cumulative flow reaches ≥ 0
pm.ini.bc.viable: NPV > 0: the project creates value at the given rate.
pm.ini.bc.notViable: NPV ≤ 0: at a rate of {rate} the project is not economically justified.
pm.ini.bc.irrAbove: IRR of {irr}, above the {rate} rate: confirms viability.
pm.ini.bc.theory: Benefit methods in project selection: for NPV, higher is better and NPV > 0 is viable; IRR must exceed the minimum attractive rate; for payback, shorter is better — don't swap them.
pm.ini.gate.title: Demand gate
pm.ini.gate.subtitle: Exit criteria of the Demand phase, evaluated by the system from the project.
pm.ini.gate.allOk: All exit criteria met: the gate can go to the governance decision.
pm.ini.gate.fix.TAP_APROVADO: Record the charter approval by a sponsor who is not the PM (Project charter section).
pm.ini.gate.fix.BUSINESS_CASE_VIAVEL: Review the business case: with investment and returns, the NPV must be positive.
pm.ini.gate.fix.ALINHAMENTO_ESTRATEGICO: Link at least one project objective to a strategic goal.
pm.ini.gate.fix.GUT_AVALIADA: Prioritize the demand with the GUT matrix (gravity × urgency × trend).
pm.ini.gate.fix.PARTES_INTERESSADAS_MAPE: Register the stakeholders (power × interest) — on the canvas, Stakeholders block.
pm.ini.gate.noRecord: Decided without a DECIA record: governance decides and holds to account — record the decision and its rationale.
pm.ini.gate.notDecided: The gate has not been decided yet.
pm.ini.gate.theory: Each phase ends at a gate with verifiable exit criteria. Passing or not is a governance decision (evaluate, direct, monitor); the work inside the phase is management.
pm.gov.subtitle: Who decides what: governance evaluates, directs and monitors; management plans and does. Goals cascade, prioritization, budget, authority, principles and the decisions in DECIA.
pm.gov.metricsHint: The same numbers as the AI feedback, computed from the project.
pm.gov.gx.title: Governance × management
pm.gov.gx.governanceQ: Are we doing the right things? The board and senior management evaluate, direct and monitor (ISO/IEC 38500 EDM model).
pm.gov.gx.managementQ: Are we doing things the right way? Executives, the PM and the team plan, build, run and monitor.
pm.gov.gx.theory: Governance decides and holds to account; management plans and does. Only COBIT's EDM domain is governance — MEA monitors execution but is management. Approving the IT budget is governance; spending it is management.
pm.gov.who.title: Who decides what in the workspace
pm.gov.who.caption: Project decisions: who decides, where it is recorded and its nature (governance or management)
pm.gov.who.row.selection: Select and prioritize the project (GUT, AHP, business case)
pm.gov.who.row.gate: Pass the phase gate: advance, with conditions, hold or terminate
pm.gov.who.row.changeNormal: Approve or reject a normal change (scope, schedule, cost)
pm.gov.who.row.work: Plan and execute the work: WBS, schedule, risks, earned value
pm.gov.cascade.title: Goals cascade
pm.gov.cascade.subtitle: Top-down: corporate goals (strategic plan, BSC) → IT goals (IT master plan) → project objectives in the charter.
pm.gov.cascade.theory: No IT target is born on its own: it derives from a corporate goal. The direction is always top-down — IT goals do not determine corporate ones, and the two are not at the same level.
pm.gov.goals.title: Strategic goals
pm.gov.goals.empty: No strategic goals yet: bring in the goals of the strategic plan, IT master plan or BSC.
pm.gov.goals.needCodeText: Enter the strategic goal's code and text.
pm.gov.goals.duplicate: There is already a strategic goal with code {code}.
pm.gov.align.title: Project objectives × strategic goal
pm.gov.align.caption: Each project objective (charter), the strategic goal it serves and the alignment
pm.gov.align.noObjectives: The charter has no objectives yet: write them in Initiating.
pm.gov.gut.title: Demand prioritization (GUT)
pm.gov.gut.subtitle: Scores from 1 to 5 for gravity, urgency and trend; the priority is the product G × U × T.
pm.gov.gut.uHint: Time available before the problem gets worse.
pm.gov.gut.tHint: How much the problem grows over time.
pm.gov.gut.pending: Choose G, U and T to compute the priority.
pm.gov.gut.notAssessed: Demand not prioritized yet: the Demand gate requires the GUT matrix.
pm.gov.gut.theory: Priority is the product G × U × T, never the sum. In the IT master plan, the GUT matrix prioritizes the needs inventory alongside strategic alignment, risk and cost.
pm.gov.need.label: Type of need (IT master plan inventory)
pm.gov.need.hint: The needs inventory belongs to the IT master plan's Diagnosis: information, services, infrastructure, procurement and staff.
pm.gov.rgt.title: Run · Grow · Transform
pm.gov.rgt.subtitle: Executive reading of the budget: how much keeps what exists, how much grows and how much transforms.
pm.gov.rgt.classHint.RUN: Keeps what exists: licenses, support, infrastructure, corrective maintenance.
pm.gov.rgt.classHint.GROW: Expands the current business: more capacity, new modules, more users.
pm.gov.rgt.classHint.TRANSFORM: Creates the new business: new models, channels and revenue streams.
pm.gov.rgt.caption: Project budget lines with amount and Run, Grow or Transform class
pm.gov.rgt.col.title: Item
pm.gov.rgt.empty: No budget lines: split the project cost across Run, Grow and Transform.
pm.gov.rgt.reference: Market reference: Run ~65–70%, Grow ~20%, Transform ~10% — not a universal target; it varies with the sector and McFarlan's grid.
pm.gov.rgt.within: Within the charter budget ({diff} to spare).
pm.gov.rgt.over: Over the charter budget by {diff}: review the lines or take the change to the committee.
pm.gov.rgt.equal: Equal to the charter summary budget.
pm.gov.rgt.noTap: The charter has no summary budget yet.
pm.gov.rgt.theory: Run/Grow/Transform answers the board's question: are we just paying for maintenance or building the future? The larger the Run share, the less IT can sustain the strategy.
pm.gov.org.title: Organizational structure and PM authority
pm.gov.org.label: Organizational structure
pm.gov.org.current: {structure} structure — PM authority: {authority}; who controls the budget: {owner}.
pm.gov.org.weak: With little formal authority, the PM coordinates without power over resources: agree with the functional manager who releases people and budget.
pm.gov.org.theory: The closer to projectized, the more power the PM has over resources and budget; in a pure functional structure the PM is almost a coordinator with no formal authority.
pm.gov.iso.title: ISO/IEC 38500 principles
pm.gov.iso.hint.RESPONSABILIDADE: Roles and responsibilities for IT clearly understood and accepted.
pm.gov.iso.hint.ESTRATEGIA: Business strategy takes current and future IT capabilities into account.
pm.gov.iso.hint.AQUISICAO: IT acquisitions made for valid reasons, with clear and balanced analysis.
pm.gov.iso.hint.DESEMPENHO: IT is fit for purpose, with the required service level and quality.
pm.gov.iso.hint.CONFORMIDADE: IT complies with mandatory legislation and regulations (e.g. data protection law).
pm.gov.iso.hint.COMPORTAMENTO_HUMANO: Policies and practices respect the people involved in the processes.
pm.gov.iso.conformityGate: Conformance not checked: it is an exit criterion of the Analysis gate.
pm.gov.iso.humanForgotten: Human behaviour not checked — the most forgotten principle (and therefore the most tested).
pm.gov.iso.theory: A standard for directors, not technicians: it does not describe processes and is not certifiable. The six principles are applied through the EDM model — evaluate, direct and monitor.
pm.gov.decia.title: Governance decisions in DECIA
pm.gov.decia.subtitle: Project selection, phase gates and normal changes are decided in DECIA, with the rationale and the snapshot; the decision comes back to the workspace.
pm.gov.decia.selection: Project selection and prioritization in DECIA
pm.gov.decia.noDecia: No DECIA connection in this view: only the project's records are shown.
pm.gov.decia.none: No DECIA decision linked to this project.
pm.gov.decia.gatesCaption: Phase gates already decided, the outcome and the DECIA record
pm.gov.decia.outsideDecia: A gate was decided outside DECIA: without the record, neither the rationale nor the decision-maker is kept.
pm.gov.decia.theory: Governance decides and holds to account; management plans and does. Taking every gate and normal change to DECIA preserves the rationale, the alternatives and who decided — the accountability principle.
pm.gov.ahp.title: AHP calculator (Saaty)
pm.gov.ahp.subtitle: Local simulation to weigh project selection criteria: it does not change the project. Take the weights to the selection decision in DECIA.
pm.gov.ahp.scale: Saaty scale: 1 = equal importance · 3 = moderate · 5 = strong · 7 = very strong · 9 = extreme (2, 4, 6 and 8 are intermediate).
pm.gov.ahp.level.2: between equal and moderately more important
pm.gov.ahp.level.4: between moderately and strongly more important
pm.gov.ahp.level.6: between strongly and very strongly more important
pm.gov.ahp.level.8: between very strongly and extremely more important
pm.gov.ahp.matrixCaption: Reciprocal matrix: how much more important the row criterion is than the column one
pm.gov.ahp.formula: CI = (λmax − n) / (n − 1) · CR = CI / RI, with RI = {ri} for n = {n}
pm.gov.ahp.consistent: CR < 0.10: consistent judgments — the weights can be used in the decision.
pm.gov.ahp.inconsistent: CR ≥ 0.10: inconsistent judgments — review them (if A > B and B > C, then A > C).
pm.gov.ahp.theory: AHP in four steps: build the hierarchy (goal → criteria → alternatives), compare criteria in pairs on the Saaty scale, compute the weights from the eigenvector and only accept judgments with CR < 0.10.
pm.ctl.chg.awaiting: Awaiting the committee's decision in DECIA: the outcome comes back here once it is decided.
tasks.assist.label: Area assistant
tasks.assist.fieldHint: The profession's templates, rubric, sources and sensitive data feed the check.
tasks.assist.packError: Could not load the field pack; the check continues with the area.
tasks.assist.replaceConfirm: Applying “{title}” replaces title, objective, outline, deliverables, criteria and references. Due date, owner and privacy stay.
tasks.assist.noTemplates: Pick the area or field of study to see templates.
tasks.assist.allGood: All checked: tangible goal and checkable criteria.
tasks.assist.engineNote: Checks are run by the system from the form, the area and the field pack (no AI engine connected in this version). With AI on, it comments from these same findings — it never invents criteria nor decides for you.
tasks.q.titulo.title: Title
tasks.q.titulo.why: Readers browse the collection by title; a deliverable name (noun) is easier to find than “task” or “test”.
tasks.q.titulo.warn: Short or generic title: say what will be delivered (e.g., “Service satisfaction report”).
tasks.q.tipo.title: Task type
tasks.q.tipo.why: The type defines the editor, the preview and the collection filters.
tasks.q.tipo.missing: Choose the type (document, spreadsheet, technical drawing…).
tasks.q.objetivo.title: Tangible objective
tasks.q.objetivo.why: A tangible goal is what lets you say “it's done”; it is the S, M and T of a SMART goal (project course, initiation).
tasks.q.objetivo.ok: Objective with a measure or deadline.
tasks.q.objetivo.warn: Objective with no measure or deadline: say how much and by when (e.g., “200 cases, by 11/30”).
tasks.q.objetivo.missing: Write the objective: what gets done, for whom and by when.
tasks.q.marcadores.title: Template placeholders
tasks.q.marcadores.why: Templates leave [placeholders] where only you know the value; until replaced, the task is not verifiable.
tasks.q.marcadores.warn: {n} field(s) still have bracket placeholders like [date] — replace them with real values.
tasks.q.entregas.title: Deliverables
tasks.q.entregas.why: Deliverables are nouns (WBS: work broken down into products); they are what someone receives and checks.
tasks.q.entregas.warn: “{text}” reads like an activity: name the deliverable as a product (e.g., “Test report”, not “Test”).
tasks.q.entregas.missing: Say what will be delivered (at least one deliverable).
tasks.q.criterios.title: Acceptance criteria
tasks.q.criterios.why: An acceptance criterion answers yes or no; it lets the task be reviewed, closed and measured without argument (quality and formal acceptance).
tasks.q.criterios.warn: {n} criterion(s), {vague} vague: replace words like “adequate” or “good” with a number, format, section or standard.
tasks.q.criterios.missing: Add at least two verifiable (yes/no) acceptance criteria.
tasks.q.prazo.title: Due date
tasks.q.prazo.why: Without a due date there is no schedule, no delay alert, no way to measure schedule performance.
tasks.q.prazo.warn: No due date: set one so the task enters the plan.
tasks.q.prazo.missing: High or critical priority requires a due date.
tasks.q.referenciasUrl.title: References
tasks.q.referenciasUrl.why: A reference without a link cannot be checked by the reviewer.
tasks.q.referenciasUrl.warn: {n} reference(s) without a valid address (start with https://).
tasks.q.privacidade.title: Privacy
tasks.q.privacidade.why: The access class protects the content; visibility cannot open what the class closes (data protection and access-to-information laws).
tasks.q.privacidade.missing: Restricted or confidential class does not fit company-wide or public visibility: narrow the visibility.
tasks.q.areaCampos.title: Area fields
tasks.q.areaCampos.why: Each area has data the executor needs (repository, process, standard, case number…).
tasks.q.areaCampos.warn: {filled} of {total} area fields filled: they give the task its technical context.
tasks.q.swRepositorio.title: Repository
tasks.q.swRepositorio.why: Without the repository, review cannot find the code or the change history.
tasks.q.swTestes.title: Tests
tasks.q.swTestes.why: In software, “done” includes automated tests and review by someone else (definition of done, four eyes).
tasks.q.swTestes.ok: There is a test or code review criterion.
tasks.q.swTestes.warn: No criterion mentions tests or code review.
tasks.q.swSeguranca.title: Security
tasks.q.swSeguranca.why: Vulnerabilities come in through tasks that ignored them; the OWASP Top 10 lists the most common.
tasks.q.swSeguranca.warn: The task does not mention security (secrets, OWASP, personal data).
tasks.q.admProcesso.title: Process
tasks.q.admProcesso.why: Linking the task to its process lets you measure and improve the process, not only the task.
tasks.q.admProcesso.warn: Say which organizational process the task belongs to.
tasks.q.admIndicador.title: Indicator
tasks.q.admIndicador.why: What isn't measured isn't managed: an indicator with target, source and frequency closes the PDCA cycle.
tasks.q.admIndicador.ok: There is an indicator with a numeric target.
tasks.q.admIndicador.warn: Missing an indicator with a numeric target (e.g., average time, % compliance).
tasks.q.dsFormato.title: Format and size
tasks.q.dsFormato.why: Wrong format or size forces a redo; setting them first avoids rework.
tasks.q.dsFormato.warn: Set the piece's format and size.
tasks.q.dsAcessibilidade.title: Accessibility
tasks.q.dsAcessibilidade.why: Public pieces must be accessible; WCAG 2.2 asks for 4.5:1 minimum contrast and alternative text.
tasks.q.dsMarca.title: Brand guide
tasks.q.dsMarca.why: The brand guide ensures visual consistency and avoids rejection in review.
tasks.q.dsMarca.warn: Point to the brand guide to follow.
tasks.q.pqPergunta.title: Research question
tasks.q.pqPergunta.why: The question guides method, sample and analysis; without it, research becomes loose data collection.
tasks.q.pqPergunta.warn: Write the research question as a question (ending with “?”).
tasks.q.pqMetodo.title: Method
tasks.q.pqMetodo.why: The method says how the answer will be obtained and lets someone else reproduce the study.
tasks.q.pqMetodo.warn: Set the method (e.g., survey, interview, systematic review).
tasks.q.pqAmostra.title: Sample
tasks.q.pqAmostra.why: Sample size defines the result's precision and what can be concluded.
tasks.q.pqAmostra.warn: Describe the sample with its size (e.g., “120 staff”).
tasks.q.pqReferencias.title: Research references
tasks.q.pqReferencias.why: Grounding in sources lets claims be checked and situates the study in existing knowledge.
tasks.q.pqReferencias.warn: Only {n} reference(s): research needs at least two sources.
tasks.q.pqEtica.title: Ethics and consent
tasks.q.pqEtica.why: Research with people requires free and informed consent and data processing under Brazil's LGPD.
tasks.q.pqEtica.warn: The research involves people and plans no consent or data protection.
tasks.q.mkPublico.title: Audience
tasks.q.mkPublico.why: A message for “everyone” speaks to no one; the audience drives channel, tone and indicator.
tasks.q.mkKpi.title: Indicator (KPI)
tasks.q.mkKpi.why: Without a numeric target there is no way to tell whether the campaign worked.
tasks.q.mkKpi.warn: The indicator has no number (e.g., “open rate ≥ 25%”).
tasks.q.mkConsentimento.title: Contact consent
tasks.q.mkConsentimento.why: Direct messages use personal data: they need a legal basis (consent) and an opt-out (LGPD).
tasks.q.mkConsentimento.warn: Direct channel (e-mail, messaging) with no consent or opt-out planned.
tasks.q.plHorizonte.title: Horizon
tasks.q.plHorizonte.why: The horizon separates strategic (years) from tactical and operational (weeks).
tasks.q.plMarco.title: Milestone
tasks.q.plMarco.why: Dated milestones are the checkpoints where you verify the plan is on track.
tasks.q.plMarco.warn: Give a dated milestone to track the plan.
tasks.q.plSmart.title: SMART goal
tasks.q.plSmart.why: Specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound: without number and deadline it cannot be tracked.
tasks.q.plSmart.warn: The objective needs a number and a deadline to be SMART.
tasks.q.engNorma.title: Technical standard
tasks.q.engNorma.why: In engineering, the standard defines the acceptable minimum and protects whoever signs.
tasks.q.engNorma.warn: Cite the applicable standard (ABNT NBR, ISO, NR).
tasks.q.engArt.title: Technical responsibility
tasks.q.engArt.why: Engineering or architecture technical services require a technical responsibility record (ART or RRT).
tasks.q.engArt.warn: No mention of the responsible engineer's ART (or RRT).
tasks.q.jurNumero.title: Case number
tasks.q.jurNumero.why: Unique numbering (CNJ Resolution 65/2008) lets the case be found in any court.
tasks.q.jurBase.title: Legal basis
tasks.q.jurBase.why: A legal opinion without cited provisions does not hold and cannot be reviewed.
tasks.q.jurBase.warn: Cite the legal basis (law, article, decree, precedent).
tasks.q.jurPrazo.title: Procedural deadline
tasks.q.jurPrazo.why: A missed legal deadline is preclusion: it cannot be recovered.
tasks.q.jurPrazo.missing: Legal task without a deadline: set it (procedural or administrative).
tasks.q.jurSigilo.title: Access class
tasks.q.jurSigilo.why: Party data and case strategy are restricted information (data protection and professional secrecy).
tasks.q.jurSigilo.warn: Legal task with public access: cases and party data call for restricted access.
tasks.q.campoRubrica.title: Field rubric
tasks.q.campoRubrica.why: The field rubric gathers what the profession checks in a deliverable (standards, structure, vocabulary).
tasks.q.campoRubrica.warn: The criteria cover {covered} of {total} field rubric items; add those that apply to this deliverable.
tasks.q.campoEntregas.title: Typical field deliverable
tasks.q.campoEntregas.why: Deliverables the field recognizes count as evidence of competence in the profile and career.
tasks.q.campoEntregas.warn: The deliverable doesn't match the field's typical ones; see suggestions.
tasks.q.campoFontes.title: Field sources
tasks.q.campoFontes.why: Citing the field's reference source gives the deliverable authority and eases review.
tasks.q.campoFontes.ok: Uses a reference source of the field.
tasks.q.campoFontes.warn: No reference from the field's sources (standards, councils, agencies).
tasks.q.campoDados.title: Field sensitive data
tasks.q.campoDados.why: The profession pack flags data that must never be public without anonymization (LGPD, art. 11).
tasks.q.campoDados.warn: This field handles sensitive data ({data}); public access is risky.
pm.agile.title: Agile sprint and flow metrics
pm.agile.avg: Average velocity of closed sprints: {v} d — use it to plan the next one.
pm.agile.avgNone: No closed sprint yet to compute the average velocity.
pm.agile.noSprints: Set the sprint dates to see the metrics.
pm.agile.burnDesc: Burndown: {remaining} effort days remain at the status date.
pm.agile.cfdEyebrow: From project start to the status date
pm.agile.goalPlaceholder: What value the sprint delivers (one sentence)
pm.agile.noTimebox: Sprint without dates: set the timebox (one month or less, Scrum Guide).
pm.agile.theory: Velocity is what the team delivers per sprint (an empirical planning basis, not a productivity target); the burndown shows remaining work against the ideal line; in the CFD, widening bands signal a bottleneck; by Little's Law, average lead time ≈ WIP ÷ throughput — limiting WIP shortens delivery.

connectors.title: External source connectors
connectors.intro: Bring documents from Google Drive and OneDrive — and, by link, from SharePoint and iCloud — and turn them into tasks: copied now or linked to the original.
connectors.lgpd.title: How we handle access (LGPD)
connectors.lgpd.purpose: Purpose: list the files you search for and copy or link the ones you choose. Access is read-only: nothing changes in your account.
connectors.lgpd.security: Security: you sign in on the provider's own page (OAuth 2.0 with PKCE); the token is encrypted on the server and never shown on screen or in logs.
connectors.lgpd.control: Control: only you see and use your accounts; connecting, disconnecting and importing are recorded in the audit log.
connectors.lgpd.revoke: You can disconnect at any time: the token is deleted here (and revoked at Google). Tasks already imported stay in your inventory.
connectors.purpose.GOOGLE: read and export the Google Drive files you choose (Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drawings, PDFs, Meet recordings…) to create tasks.
connectors.purpose.MICROSOFT: read and export the files in your OneDrive that you choose (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio, Whiteboard…) to create tasks. SharePoint team pages and libraries come in by link.
connectors.scope.driveReadonly: view and download your Drive files, without changing anything
connectors.scope.offlineAccess: keep access without asking you to sign in each time (refresh token)
connectors.scope.userRead: read your basic profile (name and email)
connectors.scope.filesRead: view and download your OneDrive files, without changing anything
connectors.scopesUnknown: Could not read the permission list right now; the provider shows it before you accept.
connectors.scopesNote.GOOGLE: drive.readonly is a Google restricted scope: the organization must mark the app as internal in Google Workspace or complete Google's verification.
connectors.scopesNote.MICROSOFT: Delegated permissions, no admin consent. Microsoft does not revoke access through an API: when you disconnect, also remove Work Station at myapps.microsoft.com.
connectors.disabledHint: The {provider} connector is disabled in this environment.
connectors.disabledWho: The IT team needs to set it up: register the app with the provider (client id and secret) and set the token encryption key.
connectors.account.hint.EXPIRADO: Access expired or was revoked at the provider: reconnect to import again.
connectors.account.hint.REVOGADO: Access was revoked. Reconnect or remove this account.
connectors.account.hint.ERRO: The last attempt failed. Reconnect if the error persists.
connectors.disconnectBody.GOOGLE: We revoke the access at Google and delete the token stored here.
connectors.disconnectBody.MICROSOFT: We delete the token stored here. Microsoft does not allow revoking through an API: to end it for good, remove Work Station at myapps.microsoft.com.
connectors.disconnectKeeps: Tasks already imported stay in the inventory; linked ones stop syncing.
connectors.disconnectedMicrosoft: Also remove the consent at myapps.microsoft.com.
connectors.error.EXPIRADO: The connection to the account expired or was revoked at the provider. Reconnect the account to continue.
connectors.error.DESABILITADO: This connector is disabled in this environment.
connectors.error.PROVEDOR: The provider did not respond. Try again in a moment.
connectors.error.VALIDACAO: The request was not accepted. Check the data and try again.
connectors.error.ACESSO_NEGADO: You don't have access to this account or item.
connectors.error.NAO_ENCONTRADO: We couldn't find the account or item: it may have been disconnected, deleted or moved.
connectors.error.badAuthorizeUrl: The authorization address received is not safe; the connection was cancelled.
connectors.return.okHint: You can now import from it in the task creator.
connectors.return.reasonNone: The provider gave no reason. Try connecting again.
connectors.return.reason.ACESSO_NEGADO: You didn't authorize access, or the organization blocked the app.
connectors.return.reason.ACCESS_DENIED: You didn't authorize access, or the organization blocked the app.
connectors.return.reason.CONSENT_REQUIRE: You need to accept the permissions on the provider's page. Try again.
connectors.return.reason.INVALID_SCOPE: The provider refused the requested permissions; tell the IT team.
connectors.return.reason.VALIDACAO: The provider's response didn't check out (request expired or already used). Start the connection again.
connectors.return.reason.NAO_ENCONTRADO: The connection request was not found (expired or from another session). Start again.
connectors.return.reason.CONECTOR_EXPIRA: The connection expired before it finished. Start again.
connectors.return.reason.CONECTOR_DESABI: The connector is disabled in this environment: the IT team needs to set it up.
connectors.return.reason.PROVEDOR_INDISP: The provider did not respond while exchanging the code for access. Try again in a moment.
connectors.return.reason.SERVER_ERROR: The provider is having trouble right now. Try again in a moment.
connectors.return.reason.TEMPORARILY_UNA: The provider is having trouble right now. Try again in a moment.
connectors.catalog.title: Source catalog
connectors.catalog.intro: What each app becomes in Work Station: the task type, the export formats, whether it can stay linked to the original and how it comes in today.
connectors.catalog.filter: Filter by app, task type or format
connectors.catalog.linkableHint: Linkable: the task can stay tied to the original and sync later (watch, webhook or delta).
connectors.catalog.ptBrNote: Technical details copied from the research (in Portuguese), as gathered from primary sources.
connectors.via.CONTAHint: The connector's minimum scopes (read-only Drive or Files.Read) reach this item: search in Import from… › Connected account.
connectors.via.LINKHint: Paste the share link in Import from… › Paste link: it becomes a linked task.
connectors.via.PLANEJADOHint: Needs a scope or API beyond today's minimum; meanwhile, export the file.
connectors.apple.noApi: Apple offers no public API for Pages, Numbers, Keynote, Notes and Reminders (CloudKit only reaches an app's own data). So there is no account to connect: the way in is the link and the exported file.
connectors.apple.linkBody: In the app, use Collaborate or Share › Anyone with the link › Copy link and paste it in Create task › Import from… › Paste link. The task is created linked (it keeps the address).
connectors.apple.fileBody: Export to PDF, Word, Excel or PowerPoint (File › Export To) and save it to Google Drive or OneDrive to import through the connected account. Uploading the file directly comes with task attachments (planned).
connectors.apple.caldavBody: CalDAV reading is planned; for now, export the event (.ics) or copy the text.
connectors.apple.accepted: Accepted iCloud links ({count}) and what they become:
connectors.link.intro: Works with any provider, iCloud included, without connecting an account. The task is created linked: it keeps the address and the type; the content stays with the provider and only opens for people with access to the link.
connectors.link.urlHint: An https address from Google Docs, Drive or Sites, OneDrive or SharePoint, or iCloud.
connectors.link.refused: This address is not accepted: it must be https and from one of the services listed below.
connectors.link.titleHint: Optional; you can rename it later.
connectors.link.accepted: Accepted links and what each becomes
connectors.import.teaser: Already exists elsewhere? Bring it from Google Drive, OneDrive or by link (iCloud too).
connectors.import.title: Import from…
connectors.import.description: Pick a file from a connected account or paste a link; the import creates the task and opens its details.
connectors.import.draftNote: The import creates a new task and opens its details; what you have already typed in this form is not saved.
connectors.import.doneMode.COPIADO: The content was copied into Work Station.
connectors.import.doneMode.VINCULADO: The task keeps the link to the original.

labSim.rule.EMPRESA_DONA: Only the owning Company organizes its own departments and managers.

labSim.rule.FILA_CHANCELAS: Seal queue: issuers and curators with a review scope grant on behalf of the issuer.
labSim.rule.REVISAO_DECISOES: Decision review: the manager reviews those of the sessions they run; the Company follows along.
labSim.rule.CHANCELAS: Seals and policies: only issuers create them; employees see the ones they received on their own profile.
labSim.rule.DOSSIES: Transition dossiers: Company and Manager generate and run them; employees see their own, as subject or successor; the admin views.

pacts.metrics.note: Median and p90 by nearest rank, always with the sample. Without a sample it shows “no data”, never zero. Avoided delay is not estimated: it would be counterfactual, not a proven result. No individual leaderboard.
pacts.notify.line: An unblocking pact you take part in was updated. Updates: {n} · last on {when}.
autopilot.steps.label: Autopilot steps
autopilot.steps.save: Save and open on the Desk
autopilot.demoNote: Demo: reading and proposing happen here in the browser with fixed rules (no external AI model, nothing sent to a server); the saved project lives in this tab's memory.
autopilot.manualMode: Your AI is in Manual mode: the Autopilot proposes nothing. To use it, pick another autonomy level in your preferences.
autopilot.input.title: Paste the request or upload the file
autopilot.input.textHint: Paste the whole text, header and signature included: sender, number and deadline are usually there.
autopilot.input.privacy: Up to {mb} MB. The file is read here in the browser and never sent to any server.
autopilot.input.loaded: Read: {name} ({chars} characters). Check the text above.
autopilot.input.loadedPdf: Read: {name} — {pages} page(s), {chars} characters. Check the text above.
autopilot.input.truncated: The text went over {max} characters and was cut.
autopilot.input.err.PDF_SEM_TEXTO: I couldn't read the text of this PDF: it looks like a scanned image with no text layer. Paste the content in the field above.
autopilot.input.err.PDF_CIFRADO: I couldn't read the text: the PDF is protected (encrypted). Paste the content in the field above.
autopilot.input.err.PDF_INVALIDO: The file doesn't look like a valid PDF. Paste the content in the field above.
autopilot.input.err.ILEGIVEL: I couldn't read the file. Paste the content in the field above.
autopilot.source.title: Request text
autopilot.source.hint: Use “Show in text” to highlight where each item came from.
autopilot.facts.title: Request reading
autopilot.facts.intro: What the system read from the text, by rules (no external model). Check it, fix what you need and see where each item came from; anything you change stops being a proposal.
autopilot.facts.subject: Subject (becomes the project title)
autopilot.facts.referenceDateHint: Base for deadlines in days, weeks or months.
autopilot.facts.referenceDateToday: No date in the document: today's date applies.
autopilot.facts.deadlineNone: No deadline found: enter one if there is.
autopilot.facts.deadlineKind.MES: End of the month mentioned in the document.
autopilot.facts.deadlineKind.DIAS_UTEIS: {n} business days from {from} (no weekends or national holidays).
autopilot.facts.kindHint: Decides the project area and the templates the Autopilot reuses.
autopilot.facts.deliverablesEmpty: No deliverables found: the scheme uses the request type's template. Add any that are missing.
autopilot.scheme.title: Proposed project scheme
autopilot.scheme.intro: Phases, activities, durations (PERT three-point), dependencies and deadlines proposed from the request and the area templates. Edit freely before saving: the schedule is recalculated right away by the critical path.
autopilot.scheme.startHint: The schedule runs forward from here.
autopilot.scheme.deadlineHint: With a deadline, each activity gets its due date, counted backward.
autopilot.scheme.overrun: The critical path adds up to {days} days and ends on {finish}; the request deadline is {deadline}: it overruns by {n} days.
autopilot.scheme.overrunPinned: An activity ends after the deadline set for it: it overruns by {n} days.
autopilot.scheme.overrunHint: Shorten critical activities, run in parallel what doesn't depend on each other, drop what isn't essential or negotiate the deadline with the requester.
autopilot.scheme.fits: It fits the deadline: the critical path adds up to {days} days, ends on {finish} and leaves {slack} days until {deadline}.
autopilot.scheme.noDeadline: No deadline in the request: the critical path adds up to {days} days and ends on {finish}. Enter a deadline to compute due dates backward.
autopilot.scheme.cycle: The network has a cycle: reorder the activities.
autopilot.scheme.ganttEyebrow: Engine CPM · recalculates on every edit
autopilot.scheme.ganttDesc: {n} activities; the critical path adds up to {days} days and ends on {finish}.
autopilot.scheme.phaseExcluded: Phase left out of the project ({n} activity(ies) kept, out of the schedule).
autopilot.scheme.duePinned: Fixed: works as a hard due date.
autopilot.scheme.afterFirst: The first one in the phase starts after the previous phase.
autopilot.scheme.summaryHint: Goes into the project when saved; adjust later in the Desk tabs.
autopilot.scheme.err.VALOR_INVALIDO: Invalid value: use optimistic ≤ most likely ≤ pessimistic, in days.
autopilot.save.cta: Save and open on the Desk
autopilot.save.openDraft: View on the Desk as a draft
autopilot.save.hint: Nothing is stored until you save: the proposal stays as a draft in this tab for 24 hours.
deskHome.intro: Your desk: the projects you work on, the Autopilot drafts and a shortcut to create a project. The skin and background art come from your preferences.
deskHome.emptyDesc: Create a blank project, from a template or with the Autopilot.
deskHome.footnote: Indicators computed by the system on {date}; projects live in this tab's memory (demo).
deskHome.card.overrun: The schedule runs {n} days past the deadline.
deskHome.drafts.title: Autopilot drafts
deskHome.drafts.hint: Proposals not saved yet (valid for 24 hours, in this tab only).
deskHome.draft.banner: Autopilot draft: nothing saved yet. Review phases, activities and deadlines and save to create the project.
deskHome.draft.notFoundDesc: The draft lasts 24 hours and only in this tab; it may have expired or been discarded. Generate another one with the Autopilot.
deskHome.team.title: Team projects by phase
deskHome.team.note: Board view of the team desk: this tab's projects by current phase, read-only. Real-time editing with colleagues arrives with the projects API.
projectNew.blank.title: Blank
projectNew.blank.hint: Just the title, area and approach; you build the rest on the Desk.
projectNew.field.title: Project title
projectNew.field.areaHint: The area belongs to the project, not your profession; outside IT the Desk doesn't require IT-specific governance.
projectNew.template.title: From a template
projectNew.template.hint: Ready phases and activities, built from the Library's area templates (credited); adjust on the Desk.
projectNew.template.label: Template
projectNew.template.titleHint: Without a title, the project is called “{name}”.
projectNew.template.aulaDates: The class project keeps the sample dates so the numbers match the class.
projectNew.template.aula-decia.name: Class project: DECIA Platform v1.0
projectNew.template.aula-decia.hint: The example from the IT Project Management classes, with checkable numbers (14-day critical path, EMV, earned value).
projectNew.template.tipo-ti.name: IT system or solution
projectNew.template.tipo-ti.hint: User stories, architecture decision, development, tests, security and rollout with rollback.
projectNew.template.tipo-obra.name: Engineering work
projectNew.template.tipo-obra.hint: Descriptive memorandum, SINAPI budget, physical-financial schedule, bidding, execution and inspection.
projectNew.template.tipo-servico.name: Service or process
projectNew.template.tipo-servico.hint: BPMN mapping, standard operating procedure, rollout and indicators.
projectNew.template.tipo-aquisicao.name: Procurement (Law 14,133)
projectNew.template.tipo-aquisicao.hint: Preliminary technical study, terms of reference, legal opinion, bidding and contract control.
projectNew.template.tipo-normativo.name: Regulatory act
projectNew.template.tipo-normativo.hint: Study of rules, draft, legal opinion, publication and announcement.
projectNew.template.tipo-capacitacao.hin: Training plan, classes and follow-up report.
projectNew.template.tipo-outra.name: Generic project
projectNew.template.tipo-outra.hint: 5W2H action plan, delivery execution and delivery checklist.
projectNew.autopilot.title: With the Autopilot
projectNew.autopilot.hint: Paste an email or official letter (or upload .txt, .eml, .md, .pdf) and get a complete scheme, editable before saving.
projectNew.autopilot.p1: reads sender, subject, letter number, deadline, amounts and deliverables, showing where each came from;
projectNew.autopilot.p2: proposes phases, activities with PERT three-point estimates, dependencies and backward deadlines;
projectNew.autopilot.p3: warns how many days the critical path overruns the deadline, if it does.
projectPage.notFoundDesc: Projects still live only in the browser's memory (demo): reloading the page goes back to the example. Open the sample project or create one.
projectPage.noObjective: No objective recorded in the charter.
projectPage.indicatorsHint: Computed by the system from the project model (CPM, PERT, earned value); AI only interprets these numbers.
projectPage.ind.noEvm: No actual cost or planned value yet.
projectPage.shortcut.desk: Phase board, timeline (Gantt) and free canvas of the same project, with version history.
projectPage.shortcut.simulate: What if? Deadline, cost and scope scenarios on the same schedule.
projectPage.shortcut.mirror: Project compliance with the area's laws and standards.
projectPage.history.title: Version history
projectPage.history.hint: Each structural change creates a version. Moving cards on the canvas doesn't: the adjustment stays in the current version and comes back with it.
projectPage.history.layoutMoves: {n} position adjustment(s) on the canvas in this version
projectPage.history.confirm: Go back to v{n}? The project returns to how it was — activities, deadlines, dependencies and the canvas positions of that moment. Going back becomes v{next}; nothing is lost.
projectPage.history.noSnapshot: No snapshot in this tab (version older than the session).
projectPage.canvas.saved: Position saved in the project, no new version (stays in v{n}).
